name: つじ田 神田御茶ノ水店
address_ja: 東京都千代田区神田小川町1-4 和田ビル 1F
cuisine: The original つじ田 — the shop that opened here in 2005 and made 濃厚豚骨魚介つけ麺 a Tokyo genre. Sixteen counter seats, thick noodles into a heavy pork-and-dried-fish dip, finished at the table with sudachi and coarse black pepper; ¥1,000–¥1,999, no reservations, served until it runs out.
neighborhood: Kanda-Ogawamachi 1-chōme — 27 m from Ogawamachi station (Toei Shinjuku line): out of exit A7 and 40 m to the left. The same exits serve Awajichō (Tokyo Metro Marunouchi line) and Shin-Ochanomizu (Tokyo Metro Chiyoda line), and JR Ochanomizu is a short walk north.
hours_raw: 月・火・水・木・金 11:00 - 23:00／土・日・祝日 11:00 - 21:00　■ 売り切れ次第終了　■ 定休日：不定休
gf_detail: Ruled out by the operator's own allergen statement, not just by inference. つじ田's parent オイシーズ株式会社 (Oishes) publishes a group allergy page saying 「当店の厨房設備及び商品の製造上、アレルギー食材を完全に除くことができません」, that every dish is cooked with the same utensils so ingredients not belonging to a dish can transfer, and that 「麺、スープ等の製造工場では、小麦、卵、乳成分を原材料とする商品の製造を行ってます」 — the noodle and soup plant itself handles wheat, egg and dairy. It adds that the company may decline to serve customers who react to trace amounts. On top of that the product is wheat tsukemen noodles in a wheat-shōyu-based dip. There is no gluten-free item.
vegan_detail: Not possible. The house broth is the 豚骨魚介 double soup — pork bone plus dried fish — and the standard bowl carries chāshū. No plant-based or vegetable bowl appears on the brand's menu.

roles: 創業者・店主 (founder; the brand is operated by オイシーズ株式会社 / Oishes Inc.)
chef_bio.origin: Kanda-Ogawamachi, Chiyoda-ku — this shop is the brand's birthplace
chef_bio.background: つじ田 opened at Kanda-Ochanomizu in 2005 and is the shop the company itself credits with leading Tokyo's tsukemen culture: 「味から絆へ、2005年神田御茶ノ水でオープンして以来、味へ圧倒的なこだわりで東京のつけ麺文化を牽引」. From this 16-seat counter the brand grew into a nationwide group — Kōjimachi, Shinbashi, Iidabashi, Nihonbashi-Yaesu, Shibuya Fukuras, Suidōbashi, Ningyōchō, Ōtemachi One, Kachidoki, Tōyōchō, Ikebukuro, Osaka Higobashi and Expocity, and Fukuoka airport — plus two spin-off lines, つじ田 味噌の章 (a miso-ramen specialist opened in Ogawamachi in 2009, three Tokyo shops) and 成都正宗担々麺 (a tantanmen specialist opened in Ogawamachi in 2016). The stated house principle is that the recipe is never finished: 「濃厚豚骨魚介つけ麺のパイオニアであるつじ田のこだわりは、常においしさを求めて進化を続けること」. The Kanda-Ochanomizu shop stays deliberately plain — counter only, cash with no electronic money, no reservations, unpredictable closing days, and it stops when the soup goes.
chef_bio.philosophy: 常においしさを求めて進化を続けること — keep evolving in pursuit of flavour; 「こだわりがあるからこそ、はじめてお客様に愛される」.
chef_bio.specialty: 濃厚豚骨魚介つけ麺 — the thick pork-and-fish tsukemen the brand pioneered, eaten with sudachi and coarse black pepper.

anecdotes.text: The company dates the whole tsukemen brand to this address: 「2005年神田御茶ノ水でオープンして以来、味へ圧倒的なこだわりで東京のつけ麺文化を牽引」.
Tabelog's directions are unusually precise about how close it is — out of Ogawamachi exit A7, turn left, 40 m; the station is 27 m away.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13020599 lists つじ田 神田御茶ノ水店 at 東京都千代田区神田小川町1-4 和田ビル1F, tel 03-5256-3200, coordinates 35.69522/139.76651, genre つけ麺・ラーメン, 16 counter seats, 予約不可, no cards and no electronic money, all non-smoking, hours 11:00–23:00 weekdays and 11:00–21:00 weekends/holidays with 売り切れ次第終了 and 不定休, budget ¥1,000–¥1,999, rating 3.47, homepage tsukemen-tsujita.com. The brand site confirms the 2005 Kanda-Ochanomizu founding, the 濃厚豚骨魚介つけ麺 identity, and the two sister brands (味噌の章 from 2009, 成都正宗担々麺 from 2016), both also started in Ogawamachi. The operator's allergy page at oishes.com/allergy states that allergens cannot be fully excluded, that shared utensils are used, that the noodle and soup factories handle wheat, egg and dairy, and that service may be refused to highly sensitive customers.

gf_cross_contamination.text: The operator states outright that allergens cannot be fully excluded and that the same utensils are used across the menu, so ingredients not belonging to a dish can transfer during cooking.
The noodle and soup factories that supply the shops also produce items made with wheat, egg and dairy.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: A 濃厚豚骨魚介 tsukemen dip built in the ordinary way on wheat soy sauce; no tamari or gluten-free seasoning is named anywhere on the brand site.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The defining broth is pork bone plus dried fish, and the standard bowl is served with chāshū.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The company publishes per-brand allergen tables for つじ田 (alongside 金子半之助 and 田中そば) behind an acknowledgement screen, and explicitly warns it may decline to serve customers who react to trace amounts.

positives.text: Allergen information is published brand by brand and kept current, which is more than most independent ramen shops offer — useful for a wheat-tolerant diner avoiding egg or dairy.

cultural_comfort.level: Very easy — but cash, and a queue
cultural_comfort.note: Twenty-seven metres from Ogawamachi station, so it is essentially impossible to miss: exit A7, turn left. Sixteen counter seats, no reservations, and neither cards nor electronic money are accepted, so bring cash. It closes when the soup runs out and its closing days are 不定休 rather than fixed, so check the brand site or its social accounts before making a special trip. Ordering is counter service on effectively one dish, so no Japanese is needed; the table ritual — squeeze the sudachi, grind the pepper — is worth copying from the person next to you. If you are avoiding egg or dairy rather than wheat, the operator's allergy page at oishes.com/allergy is genuinely usable.
